What is Make AI Agents?

Visual workflow automation platform with a drag-and-drop scenario builder, extended with AI Agents that can decide which of your configured scenarios to run rather than following a fixed path.

Best for

Complex, conditional automation logic that Zapier cannot express.

Main features

  • Visual scenario builder with branching, routers, iterators and error handlers
  • AI Agents that select tools/scenarios dynamically
  • Make AI Assistant for building scenarios from text
  • Make Grid for orchestrating multiple agents
  • 2,000+ app connectors
  • HTTP module for any REST API
  • data stores
  • scheduling down to one-minute intervals
  • scenario versioning and rollback.

Practical use cases

  • Multi-branch order processing with conditional routing and error handling
  • syncing data bidirectionally between systems
  • an agent that decides which internal process to trigger based on an inbound request
  • scraping and enriching data at scale.

Who is it for?

  • Operations engineers, agencies, technically-minded business users and teams needing complex conditional logic.

Pricing, free access & limits

Operation-metered subscription tiers

Plans described in the source

Free $0 with 1,000 operations/month. Core from roughly $9-10.59/mo (10,000 operations). Pro from roughly $16-18.82/mo adding custom variables, priority execution and full-text execution log. Teams from roughly $29-34.12/mo with team features and roles. Enterprise custom. AI Agent usage consumes operations plus underlying LLM token costs. Operations scale in tiers - higher volumes reduce unit cost substantially.

Free plan

Yes - permanent free plan with 1,000 operations/month.

Free trial

Yes - free trial of Pro features on signup.

Usage limits to consider

Operation-metered, where an operation is roughly one module execution. AI Agent runs consume operations plus token costs. Free tier caps at 1,000 operations/month and limits scenario execution frequency to 15-minute intervals.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Materially cheaper per unit of work than Zapier at volume
  • the visual builder handles branching, loops and error handling that Zapier struggles with
  • scenario versioning and the execution log make debugging far easier
  • the HTTP module means no integration is truly impossible.

Limitations to consider

  • Steeper learning curve than Zapier - genuinely a technical tool
  • fewer native connectors than Zapier
  • the operations model is still confusing for newcomers
  • AI Agents are newer and less mature than dedicated agent platforms
  • no self-hosting
  • Celonis acquisition raises some long-term direction uncertainty.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web
  • mobile app for monitoring

Languages

  • Interface in several languages

API access

Yes - Make API for programmatic scenario management; custom apps SDK; MCP support

Integrations and exports

  • 2,000+ connectors plus a universal HTTP/webhook module that reaches any REST API

Evaluation notes

Make is the right choice when your logic has real branching; Zapier when you need an obscure connector. Model operations carefully - iterators over large arrays consume operations per item.
